concepts.quote: First min = data[0], then i = 1, compare data[1] with min, if it is smaller min changes, then i = 2, and so on to the end; then it prints min
concepts.why: Sequences the plan correctly (initialize min from the first element before the loop, compare each later element, update only when smaller, read min after the loop), but narrates the steps of a familiar program rather than stating a purpose with a reason or reasoning beyond it.

concepts.quote: min = data[0] ... if it is smaller min changes
concepts.why: Applies assignment correctly in context: min receives data[0], and later is overwritten only when the compared element is smaller, so only min changes.
